clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old female with chronic excessive alcohol use presented with dizziness, unsteady ataxic gait, and recurrent falls. Laboratory tests showed anemia, hypokalaemia, and hypomagnesemia. Brain MRI demonstrated demyelination in the splenium of the corpus callosum and marked cerebellar atrophy. These imaging findings alongside her clinical symptoms and alcohol history supported the diagnosis of Marchiafava-Bignami disease. Vitamin B supplementation, alcohol cessation advice, and physiotherapy were recommended.
